correctness.rationale: All unit normals are reduced by symmetry to exactly two sign chambers. An independent Cauchy facet-area calculation establishes the projection-area formula. The maximizing orbit is exhaustively characterized and its squared chord distance is 2(1-a-b) for sorted zero-sum unit coordinates. In the two-positive chamber the deficit/distance-squared ratio is exactly 1/2; in the one-positive chamber it is at least the monotone function (1-a)/[2(1-2a/3)] with a<=sqrt(3)/2. Its minimum (3-sqrt(3))/8 is attained exactly by vertex-axis normals. Numerical sampling is supplementary, not used as infinite proof. The theorem separately includes maximizers, zero-coordinate boundaries, and equality directions.

value.rationale: This resolves the precise best-constant problem for the first nonplanar regular simplex in a newly published all-dimensional quantitative theorem. The coefficient strictly sharpens 1/10, is globally attained and uniquely determined away from the maximizing orbit by eight vertex-axis directions, revealing a nonlocal triangular-shadow obstruction. The object and invariant are canonical rather than an arbitrary numerical slice; the exact finite-dimensional case informs possible dimension-dependent sharp stability constants.
